title: FlowOps order event envelope
description: The wire contract of the `order.events` exchange: one message is the JSON of `app.publishers.envelope.encode_event`. Producers validate against it before changing a payload, consumers parse against it instead of importing the producer's code. Money is a string (a JSON number would be parsed as a binary float), ids are strings, and `occurred_at` is nullable because a row that was never committed has no database-assigned timestamp.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. A bump denotes a compatible (additive) change an older consumer must tolerate; a breaking change is a new event type (`order.reserved.v2`), not a bump of this field.

event_id.description: Also the AMQP `message_id`; consumers deduplicate by it.

aggregate_id.description: The order the event is about; also sent as the `aggregate_id` header.

event_type.description: Also the AMQP routing key and `type` property.

occurred_at.description: When the fact committed (the transaction timestamp), not when the relay published it.

payload.description: A JSON-ready snapshot: consumers cannot read the Order database, so everything they need travels here.

oneOf.description: `pending -> failed`: terminal, with the reason a consumer can act on.
`pending -> cancelled`: terminal, cancelled by the customer.

money.description: A decimal string with the scale the database stores; `null` means unknown, which is not the same as 0.00.

orderSnapshot.description: The fields every order event carries, so a consumer parses one shape.

status.description: The order status after the transition; kept as a plain string so a new status is not a schema change.

inventory_reservation_id.description: The Inventory reservation that holds the stock; a consumer needs it to confirm or release.

reason.description: Why the order is terminal. The set of reasons lives in the domain, not here: a new one is not a contract change.
